A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Multi-Way Representation Alignment. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and expanded appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original probing, clustering and retrieval experiments on CIFAR-100, MASSIVE, TED-MULTI, MARKET-1501 and Flickr8k, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds benchmark evaluations, robustness tests, repeated-fit results and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The core GPA construction, shared GCPA residual corrector, trust loss and inference mappings remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 adds incremental GCPA procedures: GCPA-ADD freezes the existing corrector, while GCPA-ADD-LIGHT updates the corrector after inserting a space while retaining existing GPA maps.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original datasets and adds Flickr30k image-caption retrieval and ImageNet-1k class-prompt retrieval (Appendices A.5 and C.6). It also evaluates Flickr8k under corrupted training correspondences and noisy test embeddings, substantially extending the represented data and test conditions.

E2.justification: The principal NA, PW, GPA and GCCA comparisons are retained. Appendix C.6 additionally evaluates native CLIP-B/16 as a same-split Flickr30k reference, reporting R@1/R@5 of 0.863/0.976; this comparator role differs from CLIP's use as an aligned encoder or anchor in v1.

E3.justification: New protocols include sequential expansion from 10 to 20 models using 2,500 CIFAR-100 training samples, Flickr30k clean/noisy training conditions, Gaussian test-feature perturbations, and PCA-versus-padding controls. Flickr30k explicitly uses a lighter correction setting. For retained TED-MULTI experiments, descriptions change from all ordered pairs and six directed triad pairs to evaluated language pairs, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained weak-link, correspondence-noise and trust-parameter analyses, v2 tests unsupported fragile pairs, continual addition, spectral changes, multimodal correspondence corruption, test-feature noise, CLIP-anchor dependence, dimensionality matching and candidate-model selection (Appendices A.1-A.2 and C.3-C.7). These address distinct questions about failure conditions, mechanisms and robustness.

E5.justification: v1 reports five k-means seeds and clustering standard deviations across models, but lacks uncertainty estimates for the principal retrieval results. Appendix A.7 adds 10-seed GCPA repetitions and 95% confidence intervals on three retrieval benchmarks, explicitly distinguishing deterministic GCCA estimates. Appendix A.6 also reports runtime averages over three fits.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 retain their numerical values, while v2 adds substantial new results. Examples include Flickr30k clean R@1 of 0.640 for GCPA versus 0.626 for GCCA (Table 8), and a failure case at 50% Canny corruption where GPA reaches 0.719 versus GCPA's 0.643 (Table 4). Additional results quantify sequential extension, variability, spectral structure, computational costs and robustness; these are new findings rather than improvements to the original runs.

T1.justification: The existing propositions, Theorem B.1, corollaries and proofs are substantively unchanged. Appendix A.6 adds a limited analytical complexity argument for consensus construction: O(Md) per sample, O(NMd) total time and O(Nd) storage.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: shared-universe alignment reduces the number of maps, GPA preserves geometry, and GCPA improves retrieval through consensus correction. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 extends the existing weak-consensus warning with interpretations of spectral concentration, candidate-model usefulness and corrector updates during sequential extension. Appendix G adds substantive applicability limits concerning incompatible task structure, PCA information loss and computational costs, alongside risks of transferring undesirable structure between models. This substantially develops the account of when and why alignment helps or fails.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands experimental documentation through corruption recipes, feature-noise scaling, spectral preprocessing, sequential-update details and hardware/runtime/memory disclosures, including an NVIDIA RTX A6000 in Appendix A.6. However, the implementation repository link supplied in v1 Section 4.1 disappears, and the new lighter Flickr30k correction setting is not numerically specified.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and positioning against pairwise alignment and GCCA remain essentially unchanged. Supporting citations are added for new datasets and encoders, including Flickr30k, ImageNet, wav2vec 2.0 and ALBERT. Publication and bibliographic updates to retained works do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: Most retained prose remains unchanged. v2 corrects retrieval subsection nesting, adds the Section 4.5 overview and limitations discussion, swaps the GCPA/GCCA algorithm appendices D and E, and expands acknowledgments. These are limited narrative and organizational changes rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The predominantly single-column document becomes a two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating figures, tables and equations. Nine appendix tables are added. Figure 3 is redrawn with a percentage-scaled axis and numerical bar labels, while the other existing experimental plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical credibility through retrieval confidence intervals, anchor and preprocessing controls, and explicit tests of harmful consensus and sequential extension. These address reliability and applicability questions left largely unresolved in v1, while the expanded interpretation explains important failure conditions. Removing the implementation link and leaving the lighter Flickr30k configuration unspecified weaken reproducibility, but these drawbacks are outweighed by the stronger validation and clearer applicability boundaries.
